cases.prompt: $click Release Click 0.14.0 without changing the compact contract or one-approval workflow. During active review and approved implementation, stop guessing the intent of ambiguous shell strings: add versioned argv-based inspect, mutate, and verify runners, validate their bounded capability, execute accepted argv without a shell, and fail closed on malformed requests. Keep compatible simple direct reads convenient, require approval for mutation, invalidate stale evidence after mutation, meter explicit verification classes, and serialize Hook state updates across processes. Preserve Always ON and Manual routing, per-turn bypass, one-shot implementation, content-free out-of-repository state, standard-library-only runtime, bilingual README, MIT license, and honest unsupported-coverage documentation. Update deterministic tests and evaluation guidance. Do not commit or push.
cases.approval_followup: I approve the exact staged semantic contract and its verification scale. Implement it in one shot, choose any necessary in-scope technical means, run the completion checks once, and do not ask for a replacement contract. Do not commit or push.
required_invariants: Unset mode asks once for Always ON or Manual only before the first software mutation
Always ON injects concise per-prompt routing context and gates supported software mutations without requiring an explicit mention
Manual mode preserves explicit @Click or $click activation and uninvoked fail-open behavior
Questions, explanations, and simple read-only lookups remain outside the build and review workflows
Code-review-only work uses a read-only guard without a build contract or approval
Review mode allows one useful inventory and then blocks repeated successful structured observations, a second successful root inventory, plan churn, and mutation
The developer execution contract contains the six compact areas and adds optional semantics, order, or an intermediate gate only when materially required
The compact developer contract and faithful plain-language explanation are shown before any repository mutation
The initial request is not treated as approval; implementation waits for explicit approval after display
The Hook stages a digest and passes only an identical contract
Implementation keeps the approved semantic contract fixed while allowing necessary in-scope technical choices without reapproval
A fresh contract can replace the prior one only after final verification passes for its current mutation revision, and starts with clean capability state
The verification scale is approved with the contract and its completion checks run as one final batch
Consequential assumptions are exposed in the contract instead of being collected through a serial technical questionnaire
Per-turn opt-out releases an active turn without changing the persistent preference
Compatible simple direct reads remain convenient, while pipelines and ambiguous active Bash require a structured capability request
Structured inspect rejects shell interpreters and write-capable operations and executes accepted argv without a shell
Structured mutate requires the exact approved contract and makes earlier evidence or verification stale
Structured verify uses explicit targeted, broad, or deep classes inside the approved budget
Malformed capability requests fail closed and Hook state updates are serialized across processes
The Click Hook itself keeps its standard-library-only runtime and stores no preference or gate state in the target repository
